chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ismail ibn Muhammad al-Minqari, from Yazeed ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who drinks an intoxicant and dies, and in his inside is something from it, not having repented from it, would be Resurrected from his grave confused, his jaw inclined, his saliva oozing, calling for the woe and the doom.
ai.seo_question: What is the physical and spiritual state of a wine drinker upon resurrection if they died without repenting?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) details the physical manifestation of spiritual corruption for those who die without repenting from consuming khamr, describing them as 'mukhballan' (confused/disoriented) with a slanted jaw and flowing saliva. This imagery serves as a tangible sign of their inner state, linking the consumption of intoxicants to the loss of rational faculty and the subsequent call for 'woe' (wa'il), a term frequently associated with the inhabitants of Hell in Shia exegesis.
